master_prompt:
Create an ultra-high resolution game asset sheet for a tactical hex rift map.

This is a UNIVERSAL 64-SLOT AI ORDER TEMPLATE. It is only the source sheet used for AI generation and later manual harvesting. It is NOT the final in-game composite tileset. The generated sheet may later be sliced, rotated, discarded, renamed, and reassigned by hand.

The layout, slot meanings, colors, and control rules are the same for every rift theme. Only the world theme changes.

EDGE NUMBERING FOR PATH SLOTS:
Use six hex sides numbered clockwise from the upper-right edge:
1 = upper-right, 2 = right, 3 = lower-right, 4 = lower-left, 5 = left, 6 = upper-left.
On path slots, open sides are the sides without red edge wedges. Red edge wedges are closed sides.

STRICT SLOT CONTRACT:
- Tiles 1 to 30 are BLOCKER / BOUNDARY NODES. They are impassable terrain pieces used to close edges, holes, outer borders, and broken passages.
- Tiles 31 to 41 are MOVEMENT / PATH PATCH NODES. They are walkable floor path pieces. The green area is passable floor. The red edge wedges show closed/blocked sides. The open movement connectors are exactly the sides without red wedges.
- Tile 31 is a straight path open on sides 1 and 4.
- Tile 32 is a straight path open on sides 2 and 5.
- Tile 33 is a straight path open on sides 3 and 6.
- Tile 34 is a 60-degree turn path open on sides 1 and 2.
- Tile 35 is a 60-degree turn path open on sides 2 and 3.
- Tile 36 is a 60-degree turn path open on sides 3 and 4.
- Tile 37 is a 60-degree turn path open on sides 4 and 5.
- Tile 38 is a 60-degree turn path open on sides 5 and 6.
- Tile 39 is a 60-degree turn path open on sides 6 and 1.
- Tile 40 is a three-way fork path open on sides 1, 3, and 5.
- Tile 41 is a three-way fork path open on sides 2, 4, and 6.
- Tiles 42 to 45 are LEVEL TRANSITION NODES. They are walkable nodes that visually imply moving to another layer, floor, depth, cave, portal, stairs, shaft, bridge, hatch, or similar transition.
- Tiles 46 to 57 are EVENT / POINT-OF-INTEREST NODES. They are walkable rooms or spaces with a localized gameplay focus.
- Tiles 58 to 64 are MOOD / FLOOR VARIANT NODES. They are walkable spaces from the same world theme but with alternate atmosphere, material treatment, danger level, or depth-layer feeling.

STRICT COLOR CONTRACT:
- RED areas mark blocked/impassable terrain mass or closed movement sides. Convert red into thematic blocked terrain, collapsed edge, rubble, broken passage, dense obstacle, sealed structure, or closed boundary material.
- On Tiles 31 to 41, keep the green center clearly walkable and use the red edge wedges only to imply closed sides. Do not turn movement nodes into pure blockers, doors, stairs, ladders, or event rooms.
- BLACK areas appear only inside blocker nodes. Treat black as empty cutout / transparent void / missing terrain. Do not use black as painted floor inside walkable nodes.
- GREEN areas mark walkable floor. Convert green into thematic floor, room, platform, courtyard, path, chamber, or stable terrain.
- There are no blue or purple control marks in this template. Do not invent colored UI symbols.
- The WHITE background MUST remain completely pure white and untouched. This is critical for slicing.
- Do not copy numbers, labels, letters, UI marks, or prompt text into the generated art.

CRITICAL MODULARITY RULE:
- EVERY SINGLE HEX IS INDEPENDENT. Do not draw one giant continuous location spanning across multiple hexes. Each hex must be a standalone modular game piece.
- Every tile must fit cleanly inside its own hex slot.
- Do not connect artwork across tile boundaries.

CRITICAL CAMERA AND SHAPE RULES:
- CAMERA: true top-down view or very slight top-down orthographic.
- Do NOT use steep isometry.
- Do NOT draw tall standing walls that hide the floor.
- Do NOT draw thick 3D pedestals under tiles.
- Tiles must be readable as flat tactical map pieces with torn or broken edges where appropriate.
- Each hex represents a large area. Avoid giant cobblestones, square checkerboards, or oversized repeated grid tiles.

BACKGROUND RULE:
- Do NOT draw cosmos, stars, space, sky, or atmospheric background inside the white areas.
- Empty areas outside the terrain pieces must stay flat pure white.

STYLE:
- Polished, clean 2D hand-painted fantasy RPG map art.
- Rich modular terrain detail.
- Strong readability from a tactical top-down camera.

void_temple.theme_description: World theme: fragments of an old ruined stone monastery torn out of reality and suspended in a dark void. Ancient abandoned cult shrine, quiet melancholic mystery, weathered grey stone, cracked slabs, worn ritual geometry, creeping moss and ivy, faint cold mystical blue glow. Keep everything in the same ruined void-temple visual language.
void_temple.blocker_nodes: For Tiles 1 to 30, interpret blockers as broken outer borders of floating temple fragments: collapsed stone slabs, jagged cliff-like breaks, missing floor cutouts, rubble, sealed broken edges, and crumbling masonry dropping into void. Do not preserve flat red paint or red background plates. Red is only a mask instruction and must become natural stone/rubble/broken temple material. Black areas are missing terrain/cutouts only; do not paint cosmic swirls, stars, nebula, smoke portals, or decorative black vortexes inside blocker tiles. Larger red areas should become more complete blocked ruined mass, not thin scraps. Avoid tiny detached debris as the main shape; make blockers feel like solid boundary pieces.
void_temple.movement_nodes: For Tiles 31 to 41, create clean walkable temple floor path patches. The red edge wedges become closed/broken sides and the green areas stay passable. Tiles 31-33 must read as straight paths, Tiles 34-39 as 60-degree turns, and Tiles 40-41 as three-way forks. These eleven tiles are NOT level transitions and must NOT contain stairs, ladders, ramps, benches, wooden planks, doors, portals, large props, altars, traps, or event-room objects. Make the path topology readable through floor composition, aligned cracks, paving direction, dust trails, light trails, fallen columns, moss lanes, low broken edges, or architectural layout, while still feeling like a full room/platform.
void_temple.level_transition_nodes: For Tiles 42 to 45, create four distinct level-transition nodes in the same void-temple theme: one stair or ramp between floors, one dark pit or shaft downward, one glowing rift/portal/threshold, and one cave-like broken tunnel or collapsed arch passage.
void_temple.event_nodes: For Tiles 46 to 57, create varied event rooms: altars, ritual circles, caches, broken mechanisms, relic pedestals, traps, danger signs, combat-scarred floor, corrupted stones, sealed devices, or small points of interest. Keep each event integrated into the floor, not as a tall object blocking the tactical view.
void_temple.mood_nodes: For Tiles 58 to 64, create alternate floor/mood variants of the same temple: deeper lower floor, colder blue-lit chamber, mossier overgrown fragment, more cracked unstable slab, darker ritual-stained floor, rubble-heavy corridor, and ominous corrupted variant.
void_temple.colors: weathered grey stone, muted dark greens for moss and ivy, subtle cold blue magical glow, dark cracks, pale worn stone, pure white untouched background
